validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. EIA's 'Pipeline projects announced to expand Permian natural gas capacity' (todayinenergy id=53319, a US government source, wholly independent of Energy Transfer) explicitly names 'Energy Transfer's existing Oasis Pipeline' and its then-under-construction 'Oasis Pipeline Modernization Project' (completed end of 2022, +0.06 Bcf/d). Energy Transfer's own current intrastate-assets page (energytransfer.com/ops_intrastate.aspx, fetched live 2026-09-02) carries a detailed, specific description (not a generic mention) of the Oasis Pipeline as an in-service 36-inch intrastate line from the Waha Hub (Pecos County, TX) to the Katy Hub (Waller County, TX). This is not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct — Energy Transfer itself classifies Oasis under its 'intrastate transportation' segment (a transmission trunk connecting two major hubs), not gathering/processing; GGIT gas classification stands. DUPLICATE: checked against all 44 other rosters rows — no other row shares the Waha-Katy corridor or footprint; nearest candidates (Texas Intrastate System Gas Pipeline P0264, Atmos Pipeline Texas P0369, HPL System P0203) are named, separately-described Energy Transfer/other-operator assets with different mileages/hubs. No merge/relabel indicated. ATTRIBUTION/OWNERSHIP: Owner1=Energy Transfer 100% confirmed — Energy Transfer's own asset page lists 'Oasis Pipeline' among its 100%-owned intrastate systems (no partner/JV interest listed, unlike e.g. Comanche Trail or Red Bluff Express on the same page which do show partial %), and the EIA article independently identifies Energy Transfer as the pipeline's owner/operator. LOCATION: StartState/EndState = Texas/Texas confirmed (whole line lies within Texas, Pecos County to Waller County). Coverage note: opened/checked all 4 harvested wiki citations (bit.ly/2lWcvjz → resolves to energytransfer.com/ops_intrastate.aspx, live and on-topic; opletconnect.energytransfer.com/ipost/OPL/capacity/design-capacity-for-intrastates, still 200 but has been restructured into a generic cross-asset navigation index with no Oasis-specific capacity data anymore — content drift, not a dead link, so not cited; eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=53319, on-topic and cited above; eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, a generic EIA landing page that does not mention Oasis by name — a boilerplate citation, not itself an existence concern given the other 3 citations plus independent search corroborate the row). Also manually confirmed (outside the citable set, since SEC EDGAR 403s the verifier's standard UA as a bot-wall) that Energy Transfer's FY2015 10-K matches the sheet's OLD 1.2 Bcf/d / ~600-mile / 36-inch spec exactly, and its FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-19) asset table lists Oasis Pipeline at 750 miles / 2.0 Bcf/d — consistent with the live website and with a real physical expansion over time, not a website typo. Flagged as a spec concern below since it isn't independently citable.

validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL DISAGREEMENT, not a simple confirm-or-correct: the sheet's Capacity=1200.00 MMcf/d and LengthKnown=966.00 km (=600.4 mi) match Energy Transfer's OWN FY2015 10-K description of Oasis Pipeline verbatim ('Capacity of 1.2 Bcf/d... Approximately 600 miles... primarily a 36-inch natural gas pipeline') and the two 2017/2018 sources the gem.wiki page cites. But Energy Transfer's CURRENT live asset page (energytransfer.com/ops_intrastate.aspx, fetched 2026-09-02) now states, for the same named 'Oasis Pipeline': 'Capacity of 2.0 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)... Approximately 750 miles... primarily a 36-inch diameter... pipeline that extends from the Waha Hub market in Pecos County, Texas to the Katy Hub market in Waller County, Texas... bi-directional capability with approximately 1.3 Bcf/d of throughput capacity moving west-to-east and greater than 750 MMcf/d... moving east-to-west.' The EIA's 2022 'Oasis Pipeline Modernization Project' (+0.06 Bcf/d, completing end of 2022) only explains a small fraction of the ~0.8 Bcf/d capacity jump and none of the ~150-mile length increase, so a larger, separate expansion happened after GEM's 2022-10-11 update that I could not find dedicated press coverage of (searched; only turned up the operator's own current disclosures). I manually confirmed (via a compliant SEC User-Agent outside the verifier's standard one, so NOT included in proposed_refs per the citation-verification rule) that Energy Transfer's FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-19, CIK 0001276187, accession 0001276187-26-000013) restates the identical 750-mile/2.0-Bcf/d figures in its intrastate-assets table, so this is not a website typo. Both the old and new figures trace to ONE origin (Energy Transfer itself, across time), so I'm not treating this as independently corroborated at either value — hence 'concern' rather than a confident correction. Diameter (36 in) is unchanged across both vintages and is a straightforward blank-field fill (see fills).

fills.researcher_notes: EIA (2022, independent/government) describes it as Energy Transfer's 'existing' pipeline undergoing a capacity modernization (i.e. an active, in-service asset); Energy Transfer's own current page (2026) lists it as a currently in-service intrastate system with active throughput capacity in both directions. Two different origins, four years apart, both consistent with continuous operating status.
Both sources describe Oasis as a natural gas pipeline moving Permian natural gas to the Katy market; no ambiguity with NGL/oil.

Energy Transfer lists Oasis Pipeline among its 100%-owned intrastate systems (no JV partner listed, unlike Comanche Trail/Red Bluff Express on the same page, which do show partial interests) and EIA independently attributes the pipeline to Energy Transfer. No sole-operator ambiguity found.

Energy Transfer's own page names the origin as 'the Waha Hub market in Pecos County, Texas' and the terminus as 'the Katy Hub market in Waller County, Texas.' Single origin only (could not find a second source naming the specific counties, as opposed to just 'Waha'/'Katy'), so medium tier — StartState/EndState=Texas/Texas (already on the sheet) is corroborated more broadly.

36-inch diameter is stated on the current live page and (per my non-citable manual check) unchanged from the FY2015 10-K description, i.e. stable across a decade of the operator's own disclosures even as capacity/length grew — this is the one figure I'm confident did not change. Single origin (Energy Transfer) so medium, not high.

summary: Oasis Gas Pipeline (P0234) is real, correctly classified as an intrastate gas transmission line, not a duplicate of any other roster row, and correctly attributed to Energy Transfer (100%) in Texas -> Texas — confirmed via EIA (independent) + Energy Transfer's own current and historical disclosures. ONE genuine spec concern staged: the sheet's Capacity (1,200 MMcf/d) and LengthKnown (966 km/600 mi) exactly match Energy Transfer's 2015-vintage figures, but the operator's current page and FY2025 10-K both now state 2.0 Bcf/d / 750 mi (36-inch unchanged) — looks like a real, undocumented expansion since GEM's 2022-10-11 update, staged as a concern rather than auto-corrected since I only have one origin (Energy Transfer) for the new numbers. 5 refs added (Status, Fuel, Owner, Location, Diameter); no UNRESOLVED units.
